key_insight: Orthogonalized momentum can fail on nonsmooth convex problems when momentum is fixed, but becomes reliable again when momentum is adaptive and paired with vanishing step sizes.
engineering_relevance: For matrix-valued optimization in deep learning and LLM training, MAGD offers a practical replacement for Muon that preserves geometry-aware updates while improving convergence guarantees.
method: Analyze Muon under locally Lipschitz (nonsmooth) objectives using generalized derivatives.
Construct a failure example showing fixed-momentum Muon may miss the global optimum even with bounded iterates.
Introduce MAGD, which blends orthogonalized momentum with gradient information and adaptive weighting based on relative progress.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports synthetic experiments, image classification, and LLM pretraining benchmarks, plus theoretical convergence and an optimal dimension-dependent rate in convex settings.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on boundedness/regularity assumptions and on adaptive momentum plus vanishing step sizes, so naive fixed-parameter implementations may still fail.
